routes.label: Clear denominators and compare prime factors

question: How many distinct four-tuples \((a, b, c, d)\) of rational numbers are there with \[ \begin{aligned} &a\log_{10} 2 + b\log_{10} 3 \\ &\quad {}+ c\log_{10} 5 + d\log_{10} 7 = 2005? \end{aligned} \]
solution:
The rational restriction lets us turn the logarithmic equation into an equality involving integer powers of distinct primes. First, one solution is visible from
\[
\log_{10}2+\log_{10}5=\log_{10}10=1:
\]
the tuple \((2005,0,2005,0)\) works.

To prove uniqueness, suppose \((a,b,c,d)\) is any rational solution. Choose a positive common denominator \(N\), so
\[
A=Na,\quad B=Nb,\quad C=Nc,\quad D=Nd
\]
are integers. Multiply the given equation by \(N\), combine logarithms, and raise \(10\) to both sides. This gives
\[
2^A3^B5^C7^D
=10^{2005N}
=2^{2005N}5^{2005N}.
\]
Some of \(A,B,C,D\) might be negative. Moving those prime powers to the opposite side clears their denominators and produces an equality of positive integers. Unique prime factorization then requires the exponent of each prime to agree on both sides. Equivalently,
\[
A=2005N,\qquad B=0,\qquad C=2005N,\qquad D=0.
\]
Since \(N>0\), division by \(N\) forces \((a,b,c,d)=(2005,0,2005,0)\). We have exhibited this tuple and proved that every solution equals it, so there is exactly \(\boxed{1}\) four-tuple, choice B.
